17901069348612210.headline: 🌫️ “I’M HONESTLY SURPRISED WE’RE STILL ALIVE” — AIIMS DOCTOR
17901069348612210.caption:
🌫️ “I’M HONESTLY SURPRISED WE’RE STILL ALIVE” — AIIMS DOCTOR WARNS ABOUT DELHI’S TOXIC AIR

Delhi’s post-Diwali air pollution has triggered serious concern among medical experts. Dr Vijay Hadda, Professor of Pulmonary Medicine at AIIMS Delhi, has warned that prolonged exposure to the city’s polluted air poses a significant risk to public health.

Speaking about the worsening conditions, Dr Hadda said he was surprised people were still managing to live with such air quality. He also highlighted that even otherwise healthy people were reporting persistent throat irritation and respiratory discomfort.

📊 How bad is the pollution?

• On November 9, Delhi recorded an AQI of 370, in the Very Poor category.
• Several neighbourhoods crossed the 400 mark, entering the Severe category.
• On November 11, the citywide AQI improved to 299, but several monitoring stations continued to report Very Poor air.

⚠️ Why does this matter?

Air pollution is not just a seasonal inconvenience. Prolonged exposure to particulate matter can worsen asthma and other respiratory conditions and increase cardiovascular risks. Children, older people and those with existing health conditions are particularly vulnerable.

Dr Hadda also pointed out that green crackers do not eliminate pollution: they reduce emissions by only around 30%, according to his remarks.

💬 Should tackling air pollution become a year-round public health priority rather than an annual emergency response?

📰 Sources: Reuters (9 November 2026); ANI / The Economic Times (9 November 2026); Mid-Day / PTI (11 November 2026).

💔 FROM IIT M.TECH TO A ₹26 LPA PACKAGE — AND THEN A LAYOFF AT QUALCOMM

The post describes an IIT Hyderabad M.Tech graduate who reportedly cleared GATE, secured a placement at Qualcomm with an annual CTC of over ₹26 lakh, and was subsequently affected by the company's layoffs.

While the individual's story has not been independently verified, the broader layoffs at Qualcomm are real.

📉 What's happening at Qualcomm India?

• Layoffs reportedly began at the Bengaluru facility on 9 November 2026.
• Around 1,000 Indian jobs are estimated to be at risk.
• Qualcomm has approximately 20,000 employees in India.
• Engineering and R&D operations in Hyderabad, Chennai and Delhi-NCR may also be affected.

The company has not officially confirmed the final number of Indian job cuts.

🎓 Why does this matter to students?

For engineering students preparing for GATE, pursuing M.Tech degrees and targeting high-paying technology jobs, this development raises an important question:

Does a prestigious degree and a high salary guarantee career security anymore?

A strong career requires more than a college tag or an impressive package. Continuous learning, adaptability and financial planning matter too.

18109979474249405.headline: NEARLY 550 INNODATA EMPLOYEES REPORTEDLY LAID OFF IN INDIA
18109979474249405.caption:
🚨 NEARLY 550 INNODATA EMPLOYEES REPORTEDLY LAID OFF IN INDIA

A sudden workforce reduction at US-based AI services company Innodata has reportedly affected nearly 550 employees in India, with job cuts also reported in the Philippines.

According to media reports, the layoffs took place on 26 October 2026. Several employees said they began their day as usual, logged in and marked attendance, but later found themselves locked out of company laptops, official IDs and internal systems.

📌 What happened?

🔹 Nearly 550 employees in India were reportedly affected.

🔹 Employees said access to company devices and accounts was withdrawn during the workday.

🔹 Termination emails were subsequently sent to personal email addresses.

🔹 The communication reportedly cited a reduction in business assignments and operational requirements, rather than individual performance.

🔹 Job cuts were also reported among teams in the Philippines.

⚠️ Important clarification: Innodata has not publicly confirmed the reported total number of affected employees or issued a detailed public explanation.

💡 Why it matters

The incident raises serious questions about job security, transparent communication and employee support during sudden layoffs. For workers, losing access to employment records and payroll systems can make an already difficult situation even more stressful.

As AI-related businesses continue to evolve, employees also need fair communication and responsible workforce-transition practices.

📰 Sources: India Today, LiveMint, NDTV and Business Today.

📅 Reports published: 27–28 October 2026

Kress will continue serving as CFO while leading the company on an interim basis as its board searches for a permanent CEO.

18081900647733642.headline: GOLDMAN SACHS RESTRICTS AI CODING TOOLS FOR MOST TRADERS AND BANKERS
18081900647733642.caption:
🚨 GOLDMAN SACHS RESTRICTS AI CODING TOOLS FOR MOST TRADERS AND BANKERS

Goldman Sachs is tightening access to advanced AI coding tools, including Anthropic's Claude Code and GitHub, following an internal review of productivity and risk management.

According to a Bloomberg report published on November 2, 2026, the bank has limited access mainly to engineering teams, ending broader access previously available to traders and bankers.

📌 What changed?

🔹 Most traders and bankers have reportedly lost access to these coding tools.

🔹 Engineering teams continue to have access.

🔹 Specialist employees known as strats, who work across trading, quantitative research and software engineering, are reportedly exempt.

🔹 Some employees had previously used AI tools to monitor trading activity, model market movements and create reports.

💡 Why did Goldman make this decision?

A Goldman spokesperson said the company evaluates AI tools based on factors including productivity and risk management before deciding which teams are best suited to use them.

The bigger picture

This is not a ban on AI across Goldman Sachs, nor is it a reported layoff. It reflects a growing shift towards controlled enterprise AI adoption, particularly in highly regulated industries.

The question is no longer just how widely companies can deploy AI, but who should have access and how responsibly it should be used.

📰 Source: Bloomberg, Moneycontrol, NDTV Profit.

📅 Reported: 2 November 2026

18001930533042890.caption:
🚨 COGNIZANT RESTRUCTURING: UP TO 15,000 JOBS REPORTEDLY AT RISK

Cognizant is reportedly considering significant workforce reductions as part of its AI-focused transformation programme, Project Leap.

Reports published in May 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, estimated that around 12,000–15,000 jobs could be affected globally, with a substantial share of the potential impact expected in India.

📌 What is Project Leap?

Cognizant launched Project Leap to reshape its operating model, invest in AI capabilities, improve productivity and realign its workforce with changing business requirements.

📊 What does the latest update say?

In its Q3 2026 results announced on October 29, Cognizant revised the programme's expected costs to $180–250 million, including $150–200 million in employee severance and other personnel-related costs.

The company also said that employee redeployment helped reduce expected restructuring costs. However, it has not publicly confirmed a final number of affected employees.

💡 Why does it matter?

The development highlights how AI adoption and automation are reshaping the IT services industry. While companies are investing in new technologies, employees are facing uncertainty about job security, changing skill requirements and the future of traditional IT roles.

The bigger question: Will AI create more opportunities than the jobs it transforms or replaces?

💬 What are your thoughts? Is the IT sector entering a major workforce transition?

Sources: Cognizant Q3 2026 Results (29 October 2026); Moneycontrol (29 October 2026); Business Standard (1 May 2026).

18180583552445089.headline: NIT JAMSHEDPUR STUDENTS RAISE CONCERNS OVER RELATIVE GRADING SYSTEM
18180583552445089.caption:
📢 NIT JAMSHEDPUR STUDENTS RAISE CONCERNS OVER RELATIVE GRADING SYSTEM

A discussion around academic evaluation is gaining attention at the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jamshedpur.

According to a student post circulating online, students are concerned that the institute's relative grading system makes it difficult for a large number of students to secure a 9+ CGPA. The post claims that only one or two students in batches of around 100 achieve this level.

Students are reportedly seeking official grading-policy documents from other IITs and NITs to present comparative references to the institute administration.

📚 What do the official regulations say?

NIT Jamshedpur's published undergraduate regulations provide for relative grading. Grade thresholds are linked to class averages and standard deviation, with scope for academic review of grading ranges.

Why does this matter?

CGPA can influence placement shortlisting, higher education applications, scholarships and other academic opportunities. Students therefore want a grading system that is transparent, fair and academically meaningful.

The discussion raises an important question: how can institutes balance relative academic evaluation with fair opportunities for students?

💬 What is your experience with relative grading at your IIT or NIT? Share your views and official policy documents respectfully.

Note: The claim about only one or two students securing 9+ CGPA has not been independently verified.
